structures.name: Eye
structures.summary: Supports visual orientation and the detection of food, habitat features, and threats.
structures.detail: Goldspotted Rabbitfish forage in structurally complex shallow-water habitats where vision helps with navigation and feeding.

structures.name: Mouth
structures.summary: Takes in plant material and other food from the environment.
structures.detail: The small terminal mouth is suited to browsing and scraping food from surfaces.

structures.name: Nostril
structures.summary: Admits water to olfactory organs that detect dissolved chemicals.
structures.detail: Fish nostrils are used for smell, not breathing.

structures.name: Operculum
structures.summary: Covers the gills and helps move water across them.
structures.detail: The posterior edge of the gill cover is an important external landmark before a supervised gill inspection.

structures.name: Lateral line
structures.summary: Detects water displacement and nearby low-frequency vibration.
structures.detail: The lateral line helps the fish maintain position and respond to movement around it.

structures.name: Dorsal fin
structures.summary: Stabilizes the fish; its spines can deliver painful venom.
structures.detail: Rabbitfish dorsal spines must be treated as a hazard. A physical specimen may only be handled under trained supervision with appropriate protective procedures.

structures.name: Pectoral fin
structures.summary: Supports steering, braking, hovering, and fine positioning.
structures.detail: The paired pectoral fins sit immediately behind the operculum.

structures.name: Pelvic fin
structures.summary: Assists stability and carries spines that must be handled cautiously.
structures.detail: The paired pelvic fins are on the lower body. Rabbitfish fin spines may cause painful envenomation.

structures.name: Anal fin
structures.summary: Provides stability and includes venom-bearing spines.
structures.detail: Do not touch or cut around rabbitfish fin spines without trained laboratory supervision.

structures.name: Caudal fin
structures.summary: Provides the principal thrust for forward swimming.
structures.detail: The forked tail transfers side-to-side body movement into propulsion.

structures.name: Vent
structures.summary: An external opening on the rear underside used as an anatomical landmark.
structures.detail: This virtual activity uses the vent only to orient a supervised incision path.

structures.name: Gills
structures.summary: Exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide as water passes across the filaments.
structures.detail: Inspect the gills virtually by following the operculum landmark and observing the filament arrangement.

structures.name: Heart
structures.summary: Pumps deoxygenated blood toward the gills before it circulates through the body.
structures.detail: The compact heart is positioned ventrally behind the gill chamber.

structures.name: Liver
structures.summary: Processes nutrients, stores energy, and produces bile.
structures.detail: The liver occupies much of the anterior body cavity and may partly cover nearby organs.

structures.name: Gallbladder
structures.summary: Stores and concentrates bile produced by the liver.
structures.detail: The small green sac lies next to the liver and releases bile into the digestive tract.

structures.name: Stomach
structures.summary: Receives food and begins mechanical and chemical digestion.
structures.detail: Its shape and fullness vary with the specimen's feeding history.

structures.name: Intestine
structures.summary: Continues digestion and absorbs nutrients along a folded pathway.
structures.detail: Observe the coils without assuming every loop has exactly the same position in every specimen.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.summary: Supports blood-cell processing and immune functions.
structures.detail: The spleen is a compact, dark-red organ associated with the digestive tract.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.summary: Contributes to blood-cell storage and immune function.
structures.detail: The spleen is a small, dark red organ associated with the digestive region.

structures.name: Swim bladder
structures.summary: Helps regulate buoyancy and maintain depth efficiently.
structures.detail: The elongated gas-filled sac lies high in the body cavity below the vertebral column.

structures.name: Kidney
structures.summary: Filters blood and helps regulate water and dissolved salts.
structures.detail: The narrow kidney follows the dorsal body wall beneath the vertebral column.

structures.name: Gonad
structures.summary: Produces eggs or sperm, depending on the specimen.
structures.detail: Its appearance changes with sex and reproductive maturity; this illustration shows only the expected general region.

structures.name: Vertebral column
structures.summary: Forms the flexible supporting axis and protects the spinal cord.
structures.detail: The vertebral column anchors the segmented body musculature used in swimming.
